title: I’m not a programmer. I used AI to build a Pokémon autobattler, and now I need real people to tell me if it’s actually any good
author: Superautopokepets
selftext:
I’m not a programmer, at least not in the traditional sense.

A few months ago, I started messing around with AI tools because I had a very specific game in my head and no idea how to build it myself.

The idea was basically: what if Pokémon worked as an autobattler, with TFT traits mechanics?

You catch Pokémon, build a team, combine copies to evolve them, use items for special evolutions, stack type synergies, choose routes, fight Gym Leaders and try to make it all the way to the end.

What started as a small experiment got completely out of hand.

The game now has hundreds of Pokémon, evolution lines, Mega Evolutions, items, traits, type matchups, route choices, shops, bosses, a full single-player run and even a multiplayer mode.

I should be completely honest about the multiplayer part: **I haven’t properly tested it with real players yet, so I genuinely don’t know if it fully works.** It exists, it has gone through technical testing and a lot of fixes, but until actual people try it, I’m treating it as experimental.

Anyway, I’ve reached the point where I need feedback that no AI can really give me.

The game runs directly in the browser. No installation needed.

**Play it here:** [**https://peraivo.itch.io/turbo-super-auto-poke-pets**](https://peraivo.itch.io/turbo-super-auto-poke-pets)

This is a free, unofficial Pokémon fan project and is not affiliated with Nintendo, Game Freak or The Pokémon Company.

I’m also not trying to hide how it was made. AI was used heavily throughout development, especially for programming and testing. The game design, decisions, direction and endless rounds of “no, that is not what I asked you to change” were mine.

I’d honestly appreciate harsh feedback more than polite feedback.

If something is boring, confusing, ugly, broken or feels like a bad AI-generated decision, tell me.

I’ve already spent far too much time asking AI models whether the game works.

I’d really like to know what actual people think now.

comments.author: angrylittledev
comments.body: Why do people constantly go for copyrighted IP's especially the from companies like Nintendo that will sue you into oblivion for stealing from them?? Why?? There's so many other animal like creatures you can use, literally ANYTHING ELSE other than Pokemon, ANYTHING.. Like pick different types of Turds call it Turdemon, Don't Gotta Shit Em All..

replies.author: robogame_dev
replies.body:
Its wild - my theory is that people want so bad to be Indy devs, that when AI makes one aspect of that easier (getting things onscreen), they put on blinders to all the difficult things that AI is not making easier - especially differentiation and marketing.

If differentiation and marketing were hard before (and they were, this is what a “publisher” does), then they’re much harder and more important now that anyone and their cousin can clone any gameplay or concept in a day.

comments.body: Looks like any other AI slop game to me, sorry.

comments.author: Savage_PrawnYT
comments.body:
Looks like a cool project. Ignore the haters and focus on any useful critical feedback instead. Even if this used your own original monsters the Ai slop hate would be the same. There are loads of Pokémon fan games around. So don’t see why this deserves any hate just because Ai was involved. 

Keep going!
